question: What is the order of the pedestrian intervals shown in Figure 4I-4, and what minimum durations are labeled for the first and last intervals?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 4I-4 shows the pedestrian intervals in this order: the Walk Interval (steady WALKING PERSON), followed by the Pedestrian Change Interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND, with optional countdown), followed by the Buffer Interval (steady UPRAISED HAND). The first interval (Walk) is labeled with a minimum of 7 seconds, and the last interval (Buffer) is labeled with a minimum of 2 seconds. Standards (mandatory): - "A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement." - "The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time... The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used." Options (permitted): - "The countdown display is optional for Pedestrian Change Intervals of 7 seconds or less." The figure also notes "The Walk Interval may be reduced under some conditions (see Section 4I.06)" and that the Buffer Interval, which shall always be provided and displayed, "may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended." Support: - "Figure 4I-4 illustrates the pedestrian intervals and their possible relationships with associated vehicular signal phase intervals." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 depicts the sequence Walk Interval → Pedestrian Change Interval → Buffer Interval, with "7 seconds MIN.**" labeled under the Walk Interval and "2 seconds MIN." labeled at the Buffer Interval, and the Pedestrian Change Interval spanning the "Calculated pedestrian clearance time*** (see Section 4I.07)." [Image 2] Page 724 shows the same Figure 4I-4 in its page context along with Section 4I.06 text. Citations: - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Standard §4 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Support §6 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725)
gold_answer: Walk interval, pedestrian change interval, then buffer interval. The walk interval is labeled 7 seconds minimum and the buffer interval 2 seconds minimum, subject to the stated walk-interval exception.
